rows.verdict: EXACT. Line 74 of the committed file; the cpython-311 bytecode (source mtime 2023-06-04, same size) also checks FREEZE inside is_enable_to_move

rows.verdict: REPRODUCED from his code, but both arms use immovable frozen cells and the ablated arm uses a different scheduler. Under the upstream movable semantics the effect survives: 2.4 → 19.35

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: Bubble only declines swaps with frozen cells ("brick wall"); Selection's FREEZE branch only nudges the pointer
rows.verdict: FALSE for the committed source. `should_move_to` in Bubble and Insertion accepts FREEZE targets, `swap()` blocks only a frozen initiator, and Selection swaps into a frozen target when its value is smaller. In 30/30 runs a frozen cell moved

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: "Formally proved in Lean 4 Theorem 2"
rows.verdict: OVERSTATED. Theorem 2 evaluates two fixed 4-element lists by `decide` and says nothing about final error

rows.author: Dietz
rows.verdict: EXACT

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: Every adjacent swap lowers I by exactly 1
rows.verdict: TRUE in general. Our Lean proof covers every list and every position. Dietz's Lean covers one 3-element window. Among strictly downhill adjacent swaps, E rises in 11.8% (n ≤ 8, exhaustive)

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: "ΔI = −1 on every single swap"; "never move against their gradient"
rows.verdict: TRUE only for adjacent swaps. Non-adjacent swaps change I by an odd amount 1 + 2k. Empirically there were 0 uphill swaps on I in 7,308 swaps of upstream mixed B+S arrays: supported in that test, not proven in general

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: "100% deterministically downhill"
rows.verdict: Monotone descent on I holds. Determinism does not: the upstream runs differ trace to trace

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: Freeze a cell and nothing crosses it (Lean Thm 1)
rows.verdict: TRUE for immovable cells only. Thm 1 is a single-swap index lemma; the induction is in a comment. FALSE for the public code

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: The paper's ruler is E
rows.verdict: TRUE: Sortedness = (N − E)/N in `analysis/utils.py`. The paper's DG argument compares 0–3 frozen cells, which the 4-cell example does not address

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: Unique keys: aggregation rises then returns to chance; duplicate C = 2 below chance, C = 10 ≈ 0.659
rows.verdict: REPRODUCED in the upstream threaded code: C = 1 final 0.4825, C = 2 0.4625 ± 0.0155, C = 10 0.6675 ± 0.013. Port peak 0.624 is low against upstream 0.674 and the arXiv text 0.72

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: Critics predict "flat 0.50"
rows.verdict: The exact null is 1/2 − 1/N = 0.4875 at N = 80 (runs test). It holds for any sort whose permutation ignores labels, stable or not, so departures refute label-independence, not stability as such

rows.author: Dietz

rows.verdict: The paper states the efficiency hypothesis and says the duplicate result "suggests" it

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: p = 10⁻¹⁰³ for "the Thompson predictor"
rows.verdict: MISATTRIBUTED. That p is H1, the full 30-D PGLS predictor. Thompson-7 is H6 (p = 7.4e-81), with median error 0.0588 against 0.0383 for full-30

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: "The loss is in the same record as the win"
rows.verdict: INCOMPLETE. The outcome record reports 4/7 supported (2/4 primary); H2, H4 and H5 failed; the article reports H2

rows.author: Dietz
rows.claim: 93.5%–98.9% alignment along Thompson's grids "across 10,303 species"
rows.verdict: The numbers are \|cos\| of g_max vs r_max after projection: 0.935 (791 spp.), 0.989 (6,614 spp.). The 10,303-species dataset has only a raw-trait cos of 0.256. A random-subspace null on the 791-species data: median 0.728, and 16.5% of 200 random 8-D subspaces reach ≥ 0.935 (k = 7: 20%)
